0.long_answer: Bradycardia is a type of heart arrhythmia characterized by a resting heart rate of less than 60 beats per minute. In individuals with Emery–Dreifuss muscular dystrophy, various cardiac conduction abnormalities may occur, leading to a reduced heart rate and other arrhythmias. Bradycardia in this context can be a result of the underlying muscle degeneration and subsequent disturbances in the electrical conduction system of the heart.
